ai.description: This lizard reaches 5 cm snout-vent length. It is sandy-brown with a striped back and a very long, tapering tail. Key features include a pointed snout and smooth, overlapping dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Mesalina watsonana* is best distinguished by its distinctively elongated, slender tail and the presence of a single, large preocular scale that contacts the upper labials.
ai.habitat: *Mesalina watsonana* inhabits arid, sandy, or gravelly desert plains and scrublands with sparse xerophytic vegetation, typically ranging from lowlands up to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Persian Long-tailed Desert Lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects across sandy substrates during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Mesalina watsonana* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the spring and summer months, peaking between April and June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Mesalina watsonana* occurs in the arid regions of Pakistan and northwestern India (Rajasthan and Gujarat), typically inhabiting sandy or stony deserts at low elevations.
